quotes: Fourteen Jewish patients from 10 families of either Iraqi or Iranian origin with congenital myasthenia had associated facial malformations which included an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion and a high-arched palate.

Other common features were muscle weakness restricted predominantly to ptosis, weakness of facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech; mild and nonprogressive course; response to cholinesterase inhibitors; absence of antibodies to acetylcholine receptor;
decremental response on repetitive stimulation at 3 Hz but no repetitive compound muscle action potential in response to a single nerve stimulus.

variants.as_reported: two confirmed pathogenic mutations in the RAPSN gene

quotes: We report a 20-month-old boy with rapsyn deficiency. At birth, he presented with a weak cry, hypotonia, joint contractures, and facial deformity.
A muscle biopsy demonstrated myofiber atrophy in a pattern consistent with early denervation.
This study identified two confirmed pathogenic mutations in the RAPSN gene that are associated with congenital myasthenic syndrome (OMIM 608931).

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) reviewed rapsyn deficiency. They stated that most patients present in the first year and a few later in life. Nearly one-third of patients have arthrogryposis at birth or other congenital malformations, and intercurrent infections or fever can trigger respiratory crises leading to anoxic encephalopathy. The ocular ductions are intact in most patients.
quotes: Most patients present in the first year and a few in later life. Arthrogryposis at birth and other congenital malformations occur in nearly one-third of the patients. Intercurrent infections or fever can trigger respiratory crises resulting in anoxic encephalopathy.
The clinical features can suggest autoimmune myasthenia gravis but the ocular ductions are intact in most patients.

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) noted that in rapsyn deficiency, multiple synaptic contacts appear on single muscle fibers. The endplate AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency, and the junctional folds are not well differentiated. Different RAPSN mutations hinder rapsyn self-association or binding to AChR, impede agrin-MuSK-LRP4-mediated clustering of AChR, or decrease rapsyn expression.
quotes: Multiple synaptic contacts appear on single muscle fibers (figure 10B). The EP AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency and the junctional folds are not well differentiated (figure 10C and D).
Different mutations hinder rapsyn self-association or binding to AChR, impede agrin-MuSK-LRP4-mediated clustering of AChR, or decrease rapsyn expression.

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) stated that Indo-Europeans carry a common N88K mutation in RAPSN. They found no genotype-phenotype correlations, except that Near-Eastern Jewish patients homozygous for an E-box mutation (c.-38A>G) have a mild phenotype with ptosis, prognathism, severe masticatory and facial weakness, and hypernasal speech.
quotes: Indo-Europeans harbor a common N88K mutation in RAPSN.

There are no genotype-phenotype correlations except that Near-Eastern Jewish patients with a homozygous E-box mutation (c.-38A>G) have a mild phenotype with ptosis, prognathism, severe masticatory and facial muscle weakness, and hypernasal speech.

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) stated that most patients with rapsyn deficiency respond well to AChE inhibitors. Some derive additional benefit from 3,4-diaminopyridine, and some benefit from adding ephedrine or albuterol.
quotes: Most patients respond well to AChE inhibitors; some derive additional benefit from 3,4-DAP, and some benefit from the added use of ephedrine or albuterol.

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) reported that rapsyn deficiency accounted for 51 of 356 index patients (14.3%) with congenital myasthenic syndrome investigated at the Mayo Clinic between 1988 and 2014.
quotes: Rapsyn deficiency | 51 | 14.3
Classification based on cohort of congenital myasthenic syndrome patients investigated at the Mayo Clinic between 1988 and 2014

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) reviewed that rapsyn concentrates and anchors AChR in the postsynaptic membrane and is required for development of the junctional folds. Its tetratricopeptide repeats mediate self-aggregation and binding to MuSK, its coiled-coil domain interacts with AChR subunits, and its C-terminal domain binds beta-dystroglycan.
quotes: Rapsyn concentrates and anchors AChR in the postsynaptic membrane and is required for development of the junctional folds.

7 tetratricopeptide repeats are important for rapsyn self-aggregation and to bind to the cytoplasmic domain of MuSK; a coiled-coil domain interacts with long-cytoplasmic loops of AChR subunits; and a C-terminal domain binds to β-dystroglycan

notes.statement: Engel et al. (2015) listed rapsyn among the CMS proteins associated with congenital contractures and with sudden apneic episodes provoked by fever or stress. They also listed it as occasionally associated with limb-girdle and axial weakness.
quotes: Congenital contractures: Rapsyn, AChR δ or γ subunit, ChATGreater

notes.statement: Das et al. (2014) reported that pyridostigmine treatment in a boy with rapsyn deficiency, started at 16 months of age, led to a dramatic improvement in muscle tone and strength and steady resolution of joint contractures. Four months after treatment began, he was starting to bear weight, sit unsupported, and say full words.
quotes: The patient was treated with pyridostigmine at 16 months of age, which resulted in a dramatic improvement in muscle tone and strength and a steady resolution of joint contractures.
Four months after treatment was initiated, he was beginning to bear weight and was able to sit unsupported and vocalize full words.

notes.statement: Das et al. (2014) used whole-exome sequencing to diagnose rapsyn deficiency after imaging, metabolic, electrodiagnostic, microarray and muscle biopsy studies were nondiagnostic. They highlighted next-generation sequencing as an important diagnostic tool that can lead to life-saving treatment.
quotes: Based on nonspecific and nondiagnostic results, whole-exome (next generation) sequencing was performed.
This patient serves to highlight next-generation sequencing as an important diagnostic tool that can result in life-saving treatment.

notes.statement: Gaudon et al. (2010) found that multiexon deletions of RAPSN, which direct sequencing did not detect, made up 15% of their CMS patients with RAPSN mutations. They recommended using SNP markers and a gene dosage method in addition to sequencing, particularly when genetic counseling is an issue.
quotes: These three genomic rearrangements in RAPSN represent 15% of our CMS patients with RAPSN mutations and we emphasize that single-nucleotide polymorphism markers and a gene dosage method should be performed in addition to DNA direct sequencing analysis particularly when there is a genetic counselling issue.

notes.statement: Müller et al. (2004) concluded that the congenital myasthenic syndrome mutation RAPSN N88K derives from an ancient Indo-European founder.
quotes: The congenital myasthenic syndrome mutation RAPSN N88K derives from an ancient Indo-European founder.

notes.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) typed 7 intragenic SNPs spanning 8 kb of the rapsyn gene. They found a common haplotype in 3 affected N88K homozygotes and in all heterozygous carriers of N88K, which supported a founder effect for the mutation.
quotes: we used seven intragenic single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) spanning 8 kb to characterize the haplotype associated with N88K
Our findings of a common haplotype associated with the N88K mutation support a founder effect.

notes.statement: Dunne and Maselli (2004) found a second haplotype in 2 asymptomatic N88K homozygotes that differed at 3 SNP sites downstream of the mutation. They suggested that recombination events within the rapsyn gene may affect how the disease is expressed.
quotes: Of note, in two asymptomatic N88K homozygous individuals, a second haplotype was present that differed at three SNP sites downstream from the N88K mutation.

The discordant haplotype found in homozygous individuals suggests that recombination events may have occurred within the rapsyn gene and that this may have implications in the phenotypic expression of the disease.

notes.statement: Burke et al. (2003) noted 2 distinct phenotypes in patients with rapsyn mutations: an early-onset form frequently associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises, and a late-onset form developing in adolescence or adulthood.
quotes: Two distinct phenotypes were noted: early and late onset. The former is frequently associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises.
The late-onset phenotype developed in adolescence or adulthood and was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.

notes.statement: Burke et al. (2003) found that the late-onset rapsyn phenotype was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis, and stated that its recognition should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.
quotes: The late-onset phenotype developed in adolescence or adulthood and was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis. Recognition of this late-onset phenotype should prevent inappropriate immunotherapy.

notes.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) found by haplotype analysis that the RAPSN -38A-G promoter mutation, carried by Oriental Jewish patients of Iraqi or Iranian origin, arose from a common founder.
quotes: Haplotype analysis shows that -38A-->G arises from a common founder.

notes.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) determined that the major transcriptional start site of RAPSN lies 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site.
quotes: position +1 represents the major transcriptional start site that we determine to be 172 nucleotides upstream of the translational start site

notes.statement: Ohno et al. (2003) showed by electrophoretic mobility shift assays that the RAPSN -38A-G mutation gained, and -27C-G lost, binding affinity for different components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. In luciferase reporter assays both mutations attenuated reporter expression in C2C12 myotubes, and -27C-G additionally attenuated expression in MyoD- or myogenin-transfected HEK cells and markedly attenuated E-box enhancer activity on an SV40 promoter, predicting reduced rapsyn expression and endplate AChR deficiency.
quotes: Electrophoretic mobility shift assays reveal that -38A-->G gains, and -27C-->G looses, binding affinity for different components of nuclear extracts of C2C12 myotubes.

Luciferase reporter assays show that both -38A-->G and -27C-->G attenuate reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes, and that -27C-->G additionally attenuates reporter gene expression in MyoD- or myogenin-transfected HEK cells.
Impaired transcriptional activities of the RAPSN promoter region predict reduced rapsyn expression and endplate acetylcholine receptor deficiency.

notes.statement: In 4 patients with endplate AChR deficiency but no mutations in AChR subunit genes, Ohno et al. (2002) identified 3 recessive mutations in the rapsyn gene: L14P in TPR1, N88K in TPR3, and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5. N88K was present in all 4 patients, homozygous in 2.
quotes: In four patients with EP AChR deficiency but with no mutations in AChR subunits, we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5, which frameshifts in TPR5.

notes.statement: Expression studies in HEK cells by Ohno et al. (2002) showed that none of the 3 rapsyn mutations impaired rapsyn self-association, but all 3 reduced coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.
quotes: Expression studies in HEK cells indicate that none of the mutations hinders rapsyn self-association but that all three diminish coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

notes.statement: Menold et al. (1998) excluded linkage to the chromosome 2 and 17 regions that contain the AChR subunit genes, and to the 17p region where familial infantile myasthenia had been localized, in 5 Iranian Jewish families with a phenotypically unique form of CMS. Four of the families were consanguineous.
quotes: We examined these families for linkage to the regions on chromosomes 2 and 17 containing the AChR subunit genes, and to the region on 17p to which FIM was localized. Our data excludes linkage to these regions

notes.statement: Menold et al. (1998) suggested that the clinical differences among patients with CMS correlate with locus heterogeneity. They proposed that a defect in a different gene caused CMS in Iranian Jewish families, who likely carry the same ancestral mutation.
quotes: suggesting that the clinical differences seen among patients with CMS correlate with locus heterogeneity, and that a defect in a different gene is responsible for the CMS in these patients
thus it is highly likely that they would carry the same ancestral CMS mutation

notes.statement: Zlotogora (1995) noted that congenital myasthenia gravis was frequent in both the Iranian and the Iraqi Jewish communities. The Iranian Jewish community has a very high degree of inbreeding and has had strong ties with Babylonian Jewry in Iraq.
quotes: Other diseases, such as beta-thalassemia, achromatopsia, colobomatous microphthalmia, Dubin-Johnson syndrome, and congenital myasthenia gravis, were frequent in both the Iranian and Iraqi Jewish communities.
Iranian Jews represent an ancient community with a very high degree of inbreeding.

notes.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) concluded that this newly recognized form of congenital myasthenia, which showed distinctive ethnic clustering in Iraqi and Iranian Jews and was associated with facial malformations, is transmitted as an autosomal recessive disorder.
quotes: This newly recognized form of congenital myasthenia with distinctive ethnic clustering and associated facial malformations is transmitted as an autosomal recessive disorder.

notes.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) found that patients responded to cholinesterase inhibitors and had a mild, nonprogressive course.
quotes: mild and nonprogressive course; response to cholinesterase inhibitors

notes.statement: Goldhammer et al. (1990) suggested that the facial abnormalities may be secondary to the neuromuscular defect, or may be primary and unrelated to it.
quotes: The facial abnormalities may be secondary to the neuromuscular defect or may be primary and unrelated.
